page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.xlarge is an ARM64-based compute-optimized instance powered by a 2.5 GHz AWS Graviton2 processor with 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs. It features a dedicated CPU allocation with no hyperthreading, supported by 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per core ratio. The instance is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 237 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests, as well as average large-block memory bandwidth. However, the instance exhibits poor to weak performance in several areas, including a PassMark CPU score of 2694.32, a Geekbench single-core score of 932.0, and poor single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Database operations under PassMark score in the average tier, while Redis SET operations achieve a weak rating at 4.81 million operations per second.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the c6gd.xlarge leverages custom ARM architecture to deliver dedicated compute resources and high-speed local NVMe storage at a lower resource density. This hardware profile is suitable for compute-heavy workloads requiring local scratch space, such as distributed compilation, batch processing, and lightweight database operations, though it is constrained by lower memory-to-CPU ratios and weak multi-threaded decompression performance.
